newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore oil products market firmer with crudes.
newsitem.headline: Singapore oil products market firmer with crudes.

text.p: Singapore oil products firmed on crude strength, with gas oil rising on the back of a strong gas oil market in London, traders said on Tuesday.

Gas oil swaps gained 20-25 cents a barrel from Monday with October traded at $27.75-$27.76 and sellers backing away late in the day in anticipation of higher prices. IPE gas oil gained $3.50 a tonne in early trading. Traders said Asian gas oil is now about $13 a tonne below Europe and will remain supported to make up for the price lag. But physical crgoes were a tad lower with a bid at $27.50 for 150,000 barrels lifting mid-October, five cents under Monday's bid, with an offer lowered to $27.85.

India renewed its annual term deal with Kuwait at a 70-cent premium to MidEast quotes fob for diesel, up from the previous 40-cent premium. Kerosene was done at a 50-to-55-cent premium, up from the previous 30-cent premium.

Jet fuel was sold on Monday by a US trader to a European major at $29.60 a barrel for October lifting. On Tuesday, a trader bid lower for 120,000 barrels at $29.65 for Oct 20-24 facing a lower offer for Oct 20-24 lifting at $28.25. A major lowered its offer of 100,000 barrels for Oct 9-13 lifting to $29.80 fob from over $30. Nepal's kerosene tender for October delivery attracted low offers around $245 a tonne, c+f.

Naphtha firmed on the back of stronger western markets which were even attracting Indian barrels. India sold by tender two 25,000-tonne cargoes lifting October 3-5 and 7-9 at $19 per tonne below NWE quotes. Traders expected prices to soften as such high levels were deterring north Asian buying interest even as petrochemical plants returned from autumn shutdowns. Gasoline 95-octane unleaded was bid at $22.90 for October 19-23, and offered at $23.30 for October 7-21. Fuel oil was steady with 180 cst for October lifting discussed at $115/$117 a tonne. A major seemed long on supplies, while another is bidding around $116 a tonne, the trader said.--Singapore Newsroom (+65-870 3084)
